mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an attached in-law suite and an accessory dwelling unit (ADU)?

acceptedAnswer.text: While both provide separate living space for family members, an attached in-law suite connects directly to the main residence, whereas an accessory dwelling unit (ADU) is often completely independent or freestanding. An attached in-law suite typically shares utilities, central climate control, and structural walls with the primary home. An ADU, whether detached or semi-independent, usually includes dedicated utility subpanels, separate exterior entrances, full kitchen facilities, and independent living zones. Zoning allowances, HOA regulations, and lot line setbacks determine whether your property accommodates an attached suite, a detached ADU, or a garage conversion.
acceptedAnswer.description: An attached in-law suite connects directly to the primary home and shares systems, while an ADU functions as an independent dwelling with separate entrances and full utilities.
